title: Compact tenant journey shingle metrics mart
creator: Riley Thompson
description:
Summary:
Create a compact, query-efficient metrics mart that encodes tenant-level user journeys as time-shingled aggregates ("shingles") to enable fast ad-hoc slicing for Console usage and cost analysis while keeping storage costs bounded. This ticket covers the data model, ETL transformations, materialization strategy, and tests required to ship a first-class derived table for real-time SLO attribution and cost-slicing dashboards.

Background & motivation:
- Current console usage analytics require expensive wide joins across invocation, route, and session tables for cross-tenant queries; queries for short-lived ad-hoc cohorts take tens of seconds to minutes.
- We want a compact mart optimized for interactive queries (sub-3s p95) for slices by tenant, route, time-window, and feature flags while retaining per-route cost attribution accuracy within 1-2%.

Design overview:
- Model: encode user journey as fixed-size shingles (e.g., 1h, 6h, 24h windows) per tenant-route pair. Each row contains summarized metrics for a shingle: invocation_count, token_count, avg_latency_ms (approx), error_count, unique_user_hll (hyperloglog sketch), and quantile sketches for latency.
- Storage & format: parquet columnar mart partitioned by shard_key (tenant_hash mod N) and date (YYYY-MM-DD). Compact columns (use int32/int64) and base64-encoded HLL/sketch bytes for approximate population/quantiles to allow merging at query time.
- Materialization: incremental DAG (dbt models) that consumes sessionized callstream snapshots, computes shingles with watermark-driven windowing, and writes to a compact mart. Use downstream materialized view refresh nightly with micro-batches every 10 minutes for recent shards.
- Indexing & access patterns: use sparse secondary index on route_id + tenant_hash for low-cardinality fast lookups; precompute route cost attribution weights in a small dimension table to avoid repeated heavy joins.

Trade-offs considered:
- Pre-aggregate vs. raw storage: pre-aggregates reduce query latency but lose fine-grained fidelity. We chose 3 shingle granularities to allow reconstruction for most console slices without storing full raw events.
- Exact counts vs. sketches: sketches (HLL/quantile) essential to keep row width small and allow mergeable summaries. We budgeted a controlled approx error (~1-2%) and added automated tests to detect drift.
- Partitioning strategy: tenant_hash sharding reduces hotspotting for large tenants but increases cross-shard queries. Typical Console queries are tenant-scoped so this optimizes the common case.

Implementation notes & artifacts:
- Initial prototype SQL and model: dbt models under repo rw-analytics/models/console/shingle_mart.
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-analytics/pull/1287 (contains prototype SQL, performance tests, CI checks)
- Design doc and sample queries: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANALYTICS/Console+Shingle+Mart+Design
- Dashboard examples: Looker folder "console_shingle_mart_examples" and a Metabase dashboard: https://metabase.redwood.ai/public/dashboard/console-shingle-samples

Progress & recent updates:
- 2025-02-03: spike complete — prototype shingle builder produces correct HLL and quantile sketches on dev dataset.
- 2025-02-17: benchmarked on 1B-row callstream subset; incremental refresh 10-minute window writes ~120MB of parquet per shard. Query p95 for common tenant-route slices ~1.8s on analytic cluster.
- 2025-02-24: design review with PM (Anil Garg) and Observability (Priya Nair). Feedback: add automated drift alerts, tighten retention policy for 24h shingles.
- 2025-02-28: PR #1287 opened; awaiting perf review and CI flakiness fixes.
- 2025-03-04: implemented CI tests (data contract checks + sketch merge unit tests).

Open questions & blockers:
- Upstream schema change: callstream will add the new route_namespace field (ENG-40217). We must ensure backward compatibility for older rows or adapt the shingle builder when the change lands.
- Cardinality blow-up for very large tenants: need autosharding heuristic for tenants with >10k distinct routes; may require separate wide-table special-casing.
- Cost review: projected S3 storage + query costs for 12-month retention estimated at $18k/year; need Finance approval for steady-state costs.

Review feedback & next steps:
- PM feedback (Anil Garg): include a small set of prebuilt rollups for the Console landing page. Added acceptance criterion for rollups.
- Observability feedback (Priya Nair): add provenance fields (ingest_batch_id, source_version) to every mart row for auditability. Implemented in prototype.
- Data infra feedback (Sofia Martinez): prefer month-based compaction job after 30 days to reduce file count. Scheduled a follow-up (ENG-79210) to implement compaction.

Acceptance criteria (done = minimally shippable):
- dbt model exists that builds the shingle mart and passes CI on sample data.
- Incremental refresh pipeline deployed to dev cluster with 10-minute micro-batches and nightly compaction job.
- p95 interactive query for common tenant-route slices <= 3.0s in dev; sampled queries included in PR.
- Automated data-quality checks: schema validation, sketch merge unit tests, and drift alert that triggers when invocation_count deviates >5% from canonical route totals.
- Documentation: Confluence design doc and example dashboards linked in ticket.

Acceptance testing plan:
- Run A/B comparison between current wide-join queries and shingle mart queries for 50 random tenant slices; verify cost attribution delta <2% and latency improvement >2x.
- Load test incremental refresh under projected QPS for 90th percentile tenant traffic.

Next tasks (owner assignments):
- Monica Liu: finish PR perf fixes, integrate provenance fields, add monthly compaction job config (estimate 2).
- Data infra (Sofia): add autoshard heuristic proposal for large tenants (blocking for full rollout).
- PM (Anil): finance approval and rollout plan for Console paid tier (blocking if cost > budget).

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on decode/encode of sketches — ensure we use a stable serialization format so queries across releases remain mergeable.
- Cost estimates in design doc are conservative; please sanity-check against current S3 pricing and Athena/Query engine costs.

If any reviewer wants a live demo of the prototype queries on the dev cluster, ping me and I'll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough.
